Richard Cottrell

Director

Richard Cottrell co-founded Cottrell and Vermeulen Architecture with Brian Vermeulen in 1992. The practice focuses on projects in the education and community sectors and was one of only six architectural practices selected to work on the DfES Schools for the Future project. Since its establishment, it has received multiple awards, including BD Education Architect of the Year 2011, 2016 and 2018, the prestigious BD Architect of the Year Gold Award 2016.

Alongside Brian and Simon, Richard oversees the design direction of projects and has delivered a number of award-winning projects for Cottrell and Vermeulen. These include the Building Schools for the Future programme, the Westborough Primary School zero-carbon exemplar project, and the Royal London Hospital Children’s Play Space.

Richard is currently overseeing the renewal of South Dock Marina for Southwark Council, a new passive house primary school in Brent, and a new SEN children’s home in Hounslow.

Richard ran the CVA Undergraduate Architecture studio at CASS, London Metropolitan University, between 2009 and 2013 and has served as an external examiner for the University of Cambridge Department of Architecture, the University of East London, and Southbank University. Richard currently sits on the Southwark and Lewisham Design Review Panels and is co-chair of the Harrow Design Review Panel.

He was Chair of Governors at Goodrich School from 2011 to 2017.

Brian Vermeulen

Director

Brian Vermeulen co-founded Cottrell and Vermeulen Architecture (CVA) with Richard Cottrell in 1992. Before establishing CVA, Brian collaborated with Richard on the partial restoration of Le Corbusier’s Unité d’Habitation in Briey, France, having previously run his own architectural practice.

Alongside Richard Cottrell and Simon Tucker, Brian leads the practice’s design direction and has delivered numerous award-winning projects for CVA.

Brian has taught architecture at the University of Bath and London Metropolitan University and has served as a visiting critic at UEL and the universities of Sheffield, Cambridge and Brighton. His advisory roles have included membership of the Southwark Design Review Panel, work as a Civic Trust assessor and advising the Department for Children, Schools and Families on the Primary Capital Programme.

Brian also publishes an online guide to indigenous gardening in coastal Kenya, reflecting his wider interest in the interdependence of endemic plants and ecology.

Simon Tucker

Director

Simon Tucker joined Cottrell and Vermeulen Architecture in 1994 after completing his RIBA Part I, Part II and Part III at the University of Cambridge, becoming a director in 2003. The practice has focussed upon work in the education and community sectors and is currently one of only six architectural practices selected to work on the DfES Schools for the Future project. It has received multiple awards since it was established and most recently received the BD Education Architect of the Year 2016 and the prestigious BD Architect of the Year Gold Award 2016.

Alongside Richard and Brian, Simon oversees the design direction of projects and he has delivered a number of award winning projects for Cottrell and Vermeulen as project architect and project director. These include Sacred Heart School, Churchill College, Brentwood School, and Clare College, Cambridge.

Simon is currently overseeing new postgraduate housing for Churchill College, Cambridge, a new Preparatory School for Brentwood School, a Sixth Form and Dining Hall for Streatham and Clapham School and a refurbishment of the City of London Girls School in the Barbican Estate.

As a director, he is responsible for the overall running of the practice including resourcing, financial management and design direction.

Simon has successfully combined the practice of architecture with teaching as studio master at the Department of Architecture, University of Cambridge. He has continued to be involved in teaching with Cottrell and Vermeulen’s studio at London Metropolitan University and has also been a visiting critic to a number of architectural schools.

Jonathan Dawes

Associate

Jonathan joined Cottrell and Vermeulen in 2006 and became an associate in 2012.

Jonathan was project architect for the new-build sixth form centre at Brentwood School, which recently received an RIBA award. He is currently working with the school on a number of ongoing projects including Bean Library scheduled for completion in Summer 2015.

For several years he successfully combined the practice of architecture with that of teaching as studio master at the Department of Architecture and Visual Arts, University of East London where he also studied as an undergraduate. In 2006 a student under his tutelage received a commendation in the RIBA President’s Medals.

More recently Jonathan taught as Intermediate Unit Master at the Architectural Association School of Architecture in London, where he completed his Diploma studies under a full scholarship.

Jonathan’s previous experience has included work on a number of large scale new-build, fit-out and refurbishment projects including Amnesty International UK Headquarters. In addition he has also been short-listed on a number of international competitions, including an £8m social housing and master-planning project in Plaistow, East London.

Jonathan is currently a judge for the 2015 Brick Awards.

Relevant experience

Brentwood School, New Six Form Centre 2006-2011

Brentwood School- School House Refurbishment 2011-2013

Brentwood Preparatory School – feasibility and options study 2010

Brentwood School Bean Library – 2011 ongoing

Maria Westerstahl

Associate

Originally from Sweden, Maria moved to New York in 1993 where she trained at the Irwin S. Chanin School of Architecture at the Cooper Union and worked in various NY architectural practices. In 2001 Maria moved to London where she obtained her UK qualifications at the Bartlett School of Architecture. She joined Cottrell & Vermeulen in 2003 to work on the Lloyd Park Centre in Walthamstow and CVA’s exemplar scheme for the Schools for the Future. She has been an associate since 2007.

Maria is a key lead of new Southwark ADS framework project teams. Previous projects include new social housing for Southwark Council, Charter School Bermondsey, the RIBA award nominated Lyndhurst Primary School and the award winning Ann Riches Healing Space and Roof Garden at the Royal London Hospital. Maria is currently working on the South Dock Marina boatyard and catering and dining facilities at Kew College.

In 2008, she completed a self-build with partner Luke Lowings on a garage plot in North London. The space saving timber scheme is designed flexibly for nuclear and extended family life and was featured in the press and Channel 4’s “Building the Dream”.

Maria taught the second year of the M Arch course at UAL Central Saint Martins between 2019 and 2021.

Markos Spyrides

Architect

Markos joined Cottrell & Vermeulen in 2021. Prior to joining the practice, Markos assisted on a number of educational and housing projects at Childs & Sulzmann Architects as a Part 1 architectural assistant. He also spent some time at his parents’ studio in Cyprus, helping with management and administration.

Markos studied for his RIBA Part I and RIBA Part II at University of Bath, where he graduated with a first-class honours. He then went to complete his architectural education at the University of Cambridge.

Since joining Cottrell & Vermeulen, Markos has worked extensively on the Sir Michael Snyder Boarding House and other projects for Brentwood School. He has also been heavily involved in the delivery of the Sixth Form Expansion for Central Foundation Girls’ School in Bow. He has since been working on a number of projects, including the remodelling of Churchill College’s Central Concourse, proposals for new residential and agricultural buildings at Bhaktivedanta Manor, and a new Passivhaus Primary School in South Kilburn. In addition, he plays a pivotal role in preparing bids for potential tenders, assists in practice management and staff training, and leads on the practice’s BIM protocol.

Samantha Harrison

Architect

Samantha joined Cottrell & Vermeulen in 2023. Samantha is an architect with 4 years post-Part 3 experience, and a confident designer with good interpersonal and contract administration skills and construction stage experience. Samantha has experience with both residential, office and schools architecture and is an RCA practice mentor.

Previous to working with CVA, Samantha was at Squire + Partners from 2020 where she worked on a number of high-end office buildings in Central London, and prior to this from 2016 to 2020 Samantha worked with Daykin Marshall Studio on bespoke residential developments. Before qualifying as an architect, Samantha worked at Moreno Masey and also at BDP where she gained experience working on schools, housing and hospitals.

Samantha studied RIBA Part I at the University of Dundee, RIBA Part 2 at University of Edinburgh, and RIBA Part 3 at London Metropolitan University. Samantha received a distinction for RIBA Part 1, Part 2 and also for Part 3.

Since joining CVA, Samantha has been working on a new build residential project in Central London.

Romain Rihouet

Architect

Romain joined Cottrell & Vermeulen in 2023. Prior to this, he worked at Mahoco Design as a RIBA Part II architectural assistant and worked with Squire & Partners during his RIBA Part I internship in 2019/2020.

Romain completed his degree in architecture at the Architectural Association.

Since joining CVA Romain has been working on new boarding accommodation building for Brentwood School and the refurbishment of the University of Cambridge’s Churchill College campus buildings.

Lucy Guo

Architect

Lucy joined Cottrell & Vermeulen in 2026.

She completed her RIBA Part I at The University of Sydney, graduating with distinction. After completing her Part I, Lucy worked at Make Architects in Sydney, contributing to a range of residential and commercial projects.

Lucy went on to complete her RIBA Part II at The University of Edinburgh, where she was nominated for University 3DReid Prize.

Since joining CVA, Lucy has worked on a new primary school for London Borough of Brent and is currently involved in the design of a new SEN boarding house and SEN short-stay unit for London Borough of Hounslow. Lucy is fluent in English and Mandarin.

Anya Heath

Architect

Anya joined Cottrell & Vermeulen in 2026.

Prior to joining CVA, she worked at IID Architects for four years — initially while completing her architectural studies, and subsequently for two years as a qualified architect. During her time there, Anya worked on school projects across all RIBA work stages, as well as a school campus masterplan. Earlier in her career, Anya worked as an architectural assistant at AMA Chartered Architects between 2017–2018 and 2020–2021.Anya studied architecture at the University of Nottingham, where she graduated with a First-Class Master’s degree. Yasmine Dahim

Architect

Yasmine joined Cottrell & Vermeulen in 2022.

Yasmine studied for her RIBA Part I at University of Nottingham where she received a 2:1. Prior to joining the practice Yasmine worked at Apteriors as an FF&E designer on numerous school buildings. Since joining the practice, Yasmine as a part 1 architectural assistant has worked on a new Hindu temple in Harrow, a new school library in Southwark and a renovation project for a boatyard located along the river Thames.
